evidence.text:
The primary source of our liquidity is cash flow from operations. Over the most recent two-year period, our operations
have generated $5.6 billion in cash. A substantial portion of this operating cash flow has been returned to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends. We also use cash from operations to fund our capital expenditures and
acquisitions. We typically use a combination of cash, notes payable, and long-term debt, and occasionally issue shares of stock, to finance significant acquisitions.

attrs.numbers_show: CFO $2.8B both years; free cash flow not separately provided but CFO stability amid earnings decline supports conversion claim. Beneish M-score -2.64 (no manipulation flag) (E29).

attrs.management_says: Strong free cash flow conversion and disciplined focus on cash (E31, E52).
attrs.numbers_show: CFO was $2,841M → $2,807M (-1.2%, E6, E17, E24) while revenue grew 7.1%. Net income fell 17.8% ($2,131M → $1,753M, E5, E16, E24). The divergence is bridged by non-cash charges: $193M brand impairments (E38), $53M Blue Buffalo inventory purchase accounting (E51), $15M manufacturing impairments (E38), and depreciation ~$620M (E4, E15). CFO resilience matches management's cash-focus narrative.

attrs.reason: Operating cash flow was stable at $2.8B in both years (E6, E17) despite net income falling from $2,131M to $1,753M (E5, E16). The Beneish M-score of -2.64 (E29) flags no earnings manipulation. These numbers support management's claim of strong free cash flow conversion and disciplined cash focus.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: Strong free cash flow conversion is evidenced by stable operating cash flow of $2.8B in both years and a Beneish M-score of -2.64 indicating no earnings manipulation.
